beatOutlines.textOutline: They examine chooser options ('as-you-like-it'), granting the right at future date $T_1$ to choose a call or put expiring at $T_2$ ([fact-03]).

scenes.title: Knock-In Options vs. Knock-Out Options & In-Out Parity

beatOutlines.textOutline: Compare Knock-In Options: become active only if asset price touches barrier level $H$ during option life ([fact-04]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Compare Knock-Out Options: extinguish immediately if barrier $H$ is touched; In-Out Parity dictates $	ext{Knock-In} + 	ext{Knock-Out} = 	ext{Vanilla}$ ([fact-04]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Break down Cash-or-Nothing Formula: $c_{	ext{cash}} = Q e^{-rT} N(d_2)$ paying fixed cash amount $Q$ if $S_T > K$ ([fact-05]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Break down Asset-or-Nothing Formula: $c_{	ext{asset}} = S_0 N(d_1)$ paying asset value $S_T$ if $S_T > K$; vanilla call equals asset-or-nothing minus $K$ times cash-or-nothing ([fact-05]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

scenes.title: 8-Step Mastery Thread: Exotic Options & Structured Swaps

beatOutlines.textOutline: Synthesize Steps 1 to 4: Corporate exotics motivations ([fact-01]), chooser options as call-plus-put portfolios ([fact-03]), barrier in-out parity $	ext{Knock-In} + 	ext{Knock-Out} = 	ext{Vanilla}$ ([fact-04]), and binary cash/asset-or-nothing formulas ([fact-05]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Synthesize Steps 5 to 8: Asian variance dampening ([fact-07]), benchmark Asian pricing ($\$5.62$ vs $\$9.64$) ([fact-08]), P&G $\$157$M leveraged swap charge ([fact-09]), and static options replication boundary hedging ([fact-10]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

summarySteps: 1. Exotic Motivations ([fact-01]): Tailored OTC contracts providing cheaper corporate hedges and customized cash-flow matching.
2. Chooser Options ([fact-03]): 'As-you-like-it' options granting the right to choose a call or put at $T_1$, valued as call plus put.
3. Barrier In-Out Parity ([fact-04]): $	ext{Knock-In} + 	ext{Knock-Out} = 	ext{Vanilla}$ guarantees vanilla replication.
4. Binary Options ([fact-05]): Discontinuous cash-or-nothing and asset-or-nothing payoffs linked to cumulative normal probabilities.
5. Lookback Options ([fact-06]): Path-dependent contracts leveraging extreme minimums ($S_{\min}$) or maximums ($S_{\max}$).
6. Asian Options ([fact-07], [fact-08]): Price averaging dampens variance, reducing 1-year option prices from $\$9.64$ (vanilla) to $\$5.62$.
7. P&G Swap Disaster ([fact-09]): Leveraged CMT interest rate swaps triggered a $\$157$M pre-tax charge during the 1994 rate hike.
8. Static Replication ([fact-10]): Hedging exotic boundary payoffs with standard vanilla portfolios to eliminate continuous rebalancing costs.
bottomTakeaway: Exotic options and structured swaps offer customized corporate hedging and variance-dampening benefits (such as Asian price averaging), managed efficiently via in-out parity and static options replication ([fact-01], [fact-04], [fact-07], [fact-10]).
